meta.title: Targeted intrusion — living-off-the-land espionage (manufacturing OT/IT)
meta.systems: EDGE-VPN01 (SSL-VPN appliance), WEB-DMZ02 (public web/app), FS-ENG01 (engineering file server), DC-CORP01 (domain controller), WKS-ENG14 / WKS-ENG22 (engineering workstations), JMP-ADM01 (admin jump host), SQL-ERP01 (ERP database), OT-HIST01 (process historian, OT DMZ)
meta.containment: Edge VPN appliance isolated and firmware re-imaged; web shell removed from WEB-DMZ02 and host rebuilt; all domain credentials force-rotated (twice) and Kerberos krbtgt reset x2; attacker-created service accounts disabled; C2 domains sinkholed at DNS and egress IPs blocked at perimeter; OT/IT boundary firewall ruleset tightened and historian isolated for forensic imaging.
meta.narrative:
Between 1 and 20 June 2026 an unauthorised actor maintained persistent access to the corporate and OT-adjacent network of the manufacturing site. The intrusion was characterised by heavy use of living-off-the-land techniques and legitimate administrative tooling, which delayed detection and is consistent with a patient, state-aligned espionage objective rather than immediate financial gain.

Initial access was achieved on 1 June through exploitation of a known but unpatched vulnerability in the internet-facing SSL-VPN appliance (EDGE-VPN01), giving the actor an authenticated foothold without valid credentials. Within 48 hours a web shell was planted on the DMZ web/application server (WEB-DMZ02) as a resilient secondary access channel. The actor then conducted slow, deliberate discovery using built-in Windows utilities, mapped the Active Directory environment, and harvested credentials from memory on a domain-joined host.

Using pass-the-hash and stolen administrator credentials, the actor moved laterally via RDP and SMB to the engineering file server (FS-ENG01), an admin jump host (JMP-ADM01) and the domain controller (DC-CORP01), where it created two service accounts for persistence and cleared selected event logs to frustrate analysis. Approximately 60GB of engineering design data and ERP records was staged in a hidden directory and exfiltrated over an encrypted channel to cloud storage across several sessions, deliberately paced to blend with normal outbound traffic.

The intrusion was detected on 20 June when an EDR behavioural rule flagged anomalous LSASS access on WKS-ENG14, corroborated by an analyst reviewing unusual outbound volume from FS-ENG01. Containment was achieved by 22 June and full eradication and recovery, including two credential rotations and a krbtgt double-reset, completed by 30 June. There is no evidence the actor reached the OT process-control network; the process historian in the OT DMZ was accessed read-only and has been imaged for further analysis. The matter was reported to the NCSC and, on legal advice, to the ICO given the presence of limited personal data among the staged files.

govern.assets: EDGE-VPN01, WEB-DMZ02, FS-ENG01, DC-CORP01, JMP-ADM01, SQL-ERP01, OT-HIST01, WKS-ENG14, WKS-ENG22
govern.dataTypes: Engineering design files (CAD/PLM), ERP records, some employee PII, supplier contracts
govern.regs: UK GDPR / DPA 2018, NIS Regulations 2018 (OES), export-control considerations (ITAR-adjacent designs)
govern.deadlineBasis: UK GDPR Art.33 — 72h from detection (personal data among staged files)
govern.legalNotes: External counsel engaged 20 Jun. Reportable to ICO (limited PII confirmed in staged set) and to NCSC as an OES under NIS. Export-control counsel notified re: design files. Privilege asserted over technical report.
govern.secureComms: Out-of-band bridge (Signal) — corporate email assumed compromised until 22 Jun
govern.bizImpact: No production outage; engineering release schedule slipped ~1 week during forced credential rotation and DC maintenance. Estimated direct response cost £310k-£420k including external IR, overtime, legal and appliance replacement. Potential loss of competitive advantage from design-data theft assessed as high but not quantified.
govern.repRisk: High — export-controlled design theft and possible state attribution; managed via controlled disclosure. No public disclosure required beyond regulator notifications at this stage.
govern.insurance: Cyber policy CYB-88213 (Beazley). Claim opened 21 Jun, ref CLM-2026-0619. Excess £75k. Forensics covered under panel provisions.
govern.riskNotes: Primary residual risk is re-entry via undiscovered persistence. Threat-hunt sweep completed 28-30 Jun found no further footholds. OT network isolation held throughout.

custody.notes: Live memory capture from WKS-ENG14 at detection, before shutdown. Hash recorded on capture.
LSASS-dump artefact and credential-access indicators extracted. Working copy only; original write-protected.
Appliance imaged before firmware re-image. Chain documented with vendor present.
DMZ web server imaged prior to rebuild. Web shell preserved in place.
Working copy transferred to Mandiant under retainer for co-analysis. Hash re-verified on receipt.
File server imaged with staged 7z archive intact for exfil-scope assessment.
Malware samples detonated in sandbox; C2 domains and hashes shared with NCSC MISP.
OT historian imaged read-only to confirm no control-system tampering. Retained for extended OT analysis.

iocs.notes: Repeated unauthenticated requests probing the SSL-VPN appliance version endpoint from a hosting-provider ASN. Precedes exploitation by ~36h.
Vulnerability-scan pattern against the VPN appliance path known to be affected by the exploited CVE.
Actor-registered domain (registered 12 May, 20 days before use). Later resolved to C2 infrastructure. Fronted to look like a CDN.
Second staging domain used for tool download. Typosquat of a legitimate update service.
Source of successful exploitation of the unpatched SSL-VPN appliance CVE. First confirmed foothold. Authenticated session established without valid user credentials.
Malicious shared object dropped to the appliance during exploitation, providing command execution. Recovered from appliance image.
Web shell planted in the DMZ web server root as a resilient secondary access channel. Minimal, obfuscated; single-parameter command execution.
SHA-256 of the recovered web shell status_check.aspx. Shared with NCSC and Mandiant for correlation.
Web shell access URL observed being invoked from actor infrastructure. Requests blended with legitimate OWA traffic.
Living-off-the-land discovery: domain and privileged-group enumeration via built-in utilities. Low and slow.
Domain trust discovery to map the AD environment.
AdFind used for Active Directory reconnaissance — remote system and share discovery. Renamed but hash-matched to known tool.
Network configuration and host discovery from the admin jump host.
SHA-256 of a comsvcs.dll LSASS-dump artefact. Credential harvesting from memory using a signed LOLBin (living-off-the-land).
Legitimate service account whose harvested hash was abused for lateral movement. Not attacker-created; compromised.
The LSASS minidump command line via rundll32 + comsvcs.dll. Classic LOLBin credential dump.
Pass-the-hash authentication using the harvested svc-eng-backup hash, followed by RDP to the engineering file server. NTLM auth anomaly flagged in retrospect.
Internal source (WKS-ENG14) of RDP lateral movement to FS-ENG01. Internal pivot host.
SMB admin-share access used to move tooling between hosts.
RDP from FS-ENG01 onward to the admin jump host JMP-ADM01. Continued internal spread.
Attacker-created domain service account used for persistence. Named to blend with SQL service accounts.
Second attacker-created domain account, added to a privileged group. Persistence + priv-esc.
Scheduled task for persistence, masquerading as a Microsoft update task. Beaconed to C2 on a jittered interval.

iocs.value: wevtutil cl Security; wevtutil cl System
iocs.notes: Selective Windows event-log clearing on the domain controller to frustrate analysis. Partial — EDR retained telemetry.
Obfuscated/encoded payload file staged on disk; XOR-packed loader. Recovered during host imaging.
SHA-256 of the obfuscated loader p.dat.
~60GB of engineering design and ERP data staged as a split 7z archive in a hidden ProgramData path prior to exfiltration.
Archive-and-encrypt of collected data using a portable 7-Zip binary. Volume-split to ease staged exfiltration.
Primary C2 domain. Low-frequency HTTPS beaconing with jitter over the whole dwell period. Sinkholed at containment.
C2 IP that cdn-eng-sync[.]net resolved to during the intrusion. Blocked at egress on 22 Jun.
Secondary IPv6 C2 seen late in the intrusion, likely a proxy hop. Added to egress block.

iocs.value: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/121.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
iocs.notes: Beacon user-agent string, slightly stale Chrome build, used consistently by the implant. Weak indicator on its own; useful for hunting.
Staged 7z volumes exfiltrated to cloud storage fronted by the C2 domain, across several sessions timed to blend with backups.
~60GB outbound observed over encrypted transport to the C2 endpoint during the exfiltration window.
Data-transfer-size anomaly: five paced sessions totalling ~61GB, deliberately chunked below typical alerting thresholds. This volume anomaly is what an analyst corroborated at detection.
Read-only access to the OT process historian from the IT side of the boundary. No control-system interaction observed; historian imaged for analysis. Boundary held.

actions.title: Isolate EDGE-VPN01 and preserve appliance image
actions.notes: Appliance pulled from service, imaged, firmware re-flashed from known-good.

actions.title: Force-rotate all domain credentials (round 1)
actions.notes: All user + service account passwords reset; privileged accounts first.

actions.title: Double-reset krbtgt (two resets, replication between)
actions.notes: krbtgt reset twice with replication interval to invalidate any golden-ticket capability.

actions.title: Remove web shell + rebuild WEB-DMZ02
actions.notes: Shell preserved then removed; host rebuilt from image and re-hardened.

actions.title: Disable attacker-created service accounts
actions.notes: svc-mssql-hlpr and svc-net-mon disabled then deleted after evidence capture.

actions.title: Sinkhole C2 domains + block egress IPs
actions.notes: cdn-eng-sync[.]net and update-svc-msncloud[.]com sinkholed; 192.0.2.66 and IPv6 C2 blocked.

actions.title: Assess exfiltration scope from staged archive
actions.notes: ~60GB: engineering CAD/PLM, ERP records, limited employee PII, supplier contracts. Informed ICO decision.

actions.title: Enterprise threat-hunt sweep for residual persistence
actions.notes: Full estate hunt on IOCs + TTPs. No further footholds found. Documented all-clear.

actions.title: Twice-daily executive situation briefing
actions.notes: 08:00 and 18:00 exec brief during active response.

actions.title: Daily C2 sinkhole + hunt telemetry review
actions.notes: Daily review of sinkhole hits and hunt telemetry until all-clear.

escalations.reason: Domain controller compromise, attacker-created domain accounts and confirmed data staging elevate this to critical. OT-adjacency raises potential impact.
Held at critical through eradication despite containment, pending threat-hunt all-clear and confirmation OT boundary was not crossed.

notifications.notes: Reported as significant incident affecting an operator of essential services. IOCs shared via MISP.
Personal-data breach reported within 72h; limited employee PII confirmed among staged files. Ref ICO-2026-33xxxx.
Board briefed same day; twice-daily updates thereafter.
Claim opened CLM-2026-0619; panel forensics (Mandiant) engaged.
Engaged for privilege, regulatory strategy and export-control advice.
Advisory engagement via counsel given ITAR-adjacent design files in staged set.
Employees whose PII was in the staged set notified with guidance, on DPO advice.

rootCauses.detail: A known CVE in the SSL-VPN appliance had a vendor patch available 3 weeks before exploitation but had not been applied; the appliance sat outside the main patch pipeline.
rootCauses.remediation: Edge appliances brought into the managed patch programme with a 7-day SLA for critical CVEs; monthly external attack-surface review instituted.

rootCauses.factor: Flat trust between IT and engineering segments
rootCauses.detail: Once inside, the actor moved with little friction between the DMZ, engineering and domain-controller tiers; segmentation and tiered admin were weak.
rootCauses.remediation: Tiered administration model (T0/T1/T2) implemented; RDP/SMB between tiers restricted to jump hosts with MFA; network segmentation project prioritised and funded.

rootCauses.detail: LSASS access and pass-the-hash went unalerted for ~11 days; the EDR rule that eventually fired was not tuned across the engineering estate.
rootCauses.remediation: Credential-access analytics (LSASS access, PtH/NTLM anomalies) enabled and tuned estate-wide; alerting thresholds lowered for privileged hosts.

rootCauses.detail: A perception that vendor appliances were the vendor's responsibility left them under-patched; ownership was ambiguous.
rootCauses.remediation: Clear asset ownership assigned; appliance patching added to security KPIs and quarterly board reporting.

closure.notes: All containment, eradication, evidence, IOC-sharing, recovery, notification and lessons-learned steps complete. Threat-hunt all-clear documented 30 Jun. OT boundary confirmed intact. Case closed by IR lead with CISO sign-off.

lessons.attendees: Dan H, Priya S, Marcus O, Helena Marsh (CISO), Eleanor Voss (Legal), Raj Patel (DPO), Mandiant lead
lessons.well: Early evidence preservation was strong — live memory captured before shutdown gave us the credential-access picture. Out-of-band comms were stood up immediately. The OT/IT boundary held and was verified. Regulator notifications were all made within deadline.
lessons.better: Dwell time of ~19 days was too long. Edge-appliance patching was the single biggest failure. Lateral movement met almost no internal friction. Initial triage was slowed by having to correlate EDR and netflow manually.
lessons.detect: Deploy and tune credential-access analytics (LSASS access, PtH/NTLM anomalies) across the whole estate, not just servers. Add outbound data-volume anomaly alerting below the previous threshold. Correlate EDR + netflow in the SIEM automatically rather than by hand.
lessons.playbook: Add an 'edge appliance compromise' playbook covering imaging-before-reimage, firmware integrity and vendor coordination. Add a krbtgt double-reset checklist. Pre-authorise out-of-band comms and external-counsel engagement to remove start-up delay.
lessons.training: Tabletop the tiered-admin model with the infrastructure team. Brief engineering staff on living-off-the-land indicators. Run a patch-ownership workshop for appliance assets.
lessons.recs: 1) Bring all edge/appliance assets into the managed patch programme with a 7-day critical SLA. 2) Fund and deliver the IT/OT and tier segmentation project this financial year. 3) Enable estate-wide credential-theft analytics. 4) Automate EDR+netflow correlation in the SIEM. 5) Assign explicit ownership and board-level KPIs for appliance patching.
